reviews.quote: Dad's care plan was written by an actual nurse, which gave us confidence from day one. Visits are mostly reliable and the carers seem to know him properly now.
reviews.author: Margaret S.

reviews.quote: We needed help quickly after Mum left hospital. It took a few days to get the routine fully settled, but once it did, things ran smoothly. Would recommend.
reviews.author: David K.

reviews.quote: Good communication from the office and a proper assessment at the start. Not the cheapest option locally, but you can tell there's clinical oversight behind it.
reviews.author: Helen C.

reviews.quote: Dad's care plan was written by an actual nurse, which gave us confidence from day one. Visits are mostly reliable and the carers seem to know him properly now.
reviews.author: Margaret S.

reviews.quote: We needed help quickly after Mum left hospital. It took a few days to get the routine fully settled, but once it did, things ran smoothly. Would recommend.
reviews.author: David K.

reviews.quote: Eight months in and we've had the same morning carer most weeks. Mum actually waits by the door now, which says more than I can.
reviews.author: Sarah L.

personalCare.quote: Mum hated the idea of help at first. The nurse who assessed her didn't rush it, and the carer they matched has been brilliant — same person every morning for six months.
personalCare.author: Anne D.

personalCare.quote: Dad came home from hospital with fragile skin. The nurse picked up a small issue at the review visit that we'd missed. Small thing, but it mattered.
personalCare.author: Gordon R.

personalCare.quote: Took a bit longer than hoped to find the right fit in Crieff, but once sorted my wife has had consistent support. Steady routine has helped her a lot.
personalCare.author: Stuart T.

medicationSupport.quote: Dad takes seven tablets a day and doubled up on one after a mix-up. Zento sent a nurse in first, built a clear protocol, and we've had no issues since.
medicationSupport.author: Margaret H.

medicationSupport.quote: With Mum's dementia we needed more than reminders — someone who understood what each medication was for. The carer follows a proper plan, not guesswork.
medicationSupport.author: Peter F.

medicationSupport.quote: After discharge from Perth Royal, Mum's meds had all changed. Nurse assessment within 48 hours and a carer visiting that week. Huge relief for the family.
medicationSupport.author: Sheena M.

dementiaCare.quote: Carer consistency was non-negotiable for Mum — unfamiliar faces upset her. She's had the same two carers for over a year. That trust took time but it's there now.
dementiaCare.author: Janet S.

dementiaCare.quote: The nurse asked about Dad's life before dementia — his job, his routines. You can tell the carer uses that. It doesn't feel like ticking boxes.
dementiaCare.author: Michael A.

dementiaCare.quote: We were told to look at care homes but Dad wanted to stay put. Routines are calmer now. Occasional carer swap is still hard for him, but overall much better.
dementiaCare.author: Helen R.

companionship.quote: After Dad died, Mum was alone most days and wouldn't admit she was lonely. Her companion comes twice a week — crosswords, short walks. She looks forward to it.
companionship.author: Fiona M.

companionship.quote: The companion flagged that Mum had gone quiet about things she used to chat about. Turned out to be worth getting checked. That attentiveness made a difference.
companionship.author: Robert K.

companionship.quote: Dad was getting withdrawn in Livingston. Twice-weekly visits for cards and a shop run have helped. He's not suddenly social, but he's brighter.
companionship.author: Janet W.

mealPreparation.quote: Dad had lost weight and we hadn't clocked how little he was eating. Carer cooks a few times a week and sits with him. He's put a bit back on.
mealPreparation.author: Elaine C.

mealPreparation.quote: Mealtimes with Mum's dementia were a nightmare — forgetting she'd eaten, refusing favourites. Her carer found what works and stuck with it. Much calmer now.
mealPreparation.author: Douglas W.

mealPreparation.quote: Mum's appetite dropped after Dad passed. Fresh lunches a few days a week have helped. Simple thing, but she talks about food again.
mealPreparation.author: Patricia N.

hospitalDischarge.quote: Hip surgery discharge came with 48 hours' notice. I rang in a panic — nurse had a plan ready before Dad left the Royal Infirmary. Carer there when he got home.
hospitalDischarge.author: Claire B.

hospitalDischarge.quote: Mum was in Ninewells three weeks after a stroke. The nurse spoke to the ward before discharge. Meds and mobility support were in place day one. Still nerve-wracking, but handled well.
hospitalDischarge.author: Alistair D.

hospitalDischarge.quote: Knee replacement and I was dreading getting home. Coordination with the hospital was good. First week was still tough, but we weren't left on our own.
hospitalDischarge.author: George M.

respiteCare.quote: Two years without a proper break caring for my husband. Respite felt like admitting defeat — it wasn't. Handover was thorough and he barely noticed the change.
respiteCare.author: Linda P.

respiteCare.quote: Sister hospitalised, needed cover within a day. Zento had someone briefed and in place faster than expected. Properly prepared, not just a warm body.
respiteCare.author: Kenneth R.

respiteCare.quote: Five days off while my wife was looked after. Expensive but worth it. Only gripe was one late handover call — otherwise very solid.
respiteCare.author: William J.

reviews.quote: Care homes for both parents would have cost nearly double. One live-in carer let them stay in the house they've had for forty years. Not perfect every day, but right for them.
reviews.author: Fiona L.

reviews.quote: Dad's dementia and a care home felt like a bad fit. One familiar carer at home works better than a rotating ward team for him.
reviews.author: Robert T.

reviews.quote: Live-in care is a big step and a big cost. Mum's carer is capable and kind. We still visit a lot, but it's good knowing someone's there overnight.
reviews.author: Catherine B.

overnightCare.quote: Two night falls in a month — the nurse was clear Dad needed waking nights, not sleep-in. Three months on, no falls. We actually sleep again.
overnightCare.author: Rachel N.

overnightCare.quote: Nights with Mum were unpredictable. Started sleep-in, moved to waking nights after a nurse review. Sensible adjustment, not just selling the pricier option.
overnightCare.author: Andrew C.

overnightCare.quote: Dad wanders at night — we were shattered checking on him hourly. Waking carer has been a game changer. Not cheap, but nor is broken sleep.
overnightCare.author: Marion T.

twentyFourHourCare.quote: After Dad's second stroke one carer wasn't enough, especially at night. 24-hour team let him stay home. That mattered more than I can put into words.
twentyFourHourCare.author: Elizabeth W.

twentyFourHourCare.quote: Nurse was honest that live-in wasn't safe enough for Mum at night. 24-hour care blew the budget but someone awake at 3am is worth it.
twentyFourHourCare.author: Thomas G.

twentyFourHourCare.quote: We thought a care home was inevitable. The rotational team means Mum stays surrounded by her own things. Logistics are complex but well managed.
twentyFourHourCare.author: Jennifer H.

edinburgh.quote: Tried another agency first — night and day difference. Carer knows how Mum takes her tea and when she likes to get up. Three months, no care home talk.
edinburgh.author: Patricia H.

edinburgh.quote: Needed help fast after Dad's fall. Nurse assessment next day, carer by end of week. Having a nurse oversee it feels safer than a call centre.
edinburgh.author: James A.

edinburgh.quote: I manage Mum's care from London. Local team keeps me updated without me chasing. Still stressful from a distance, but much less than before.
edinburgh.author: Sandra K.

reviews.quote: Dad's fall last winter — nurse in Dalkeith spotted things we'd missed. Same carer since February. His confidence at home is noticeably better.
reviews.author: Helen B.

reviews.quote: A nurse came first, not a salesperson. Mum's had the same carer from the start. That consistency is harder to find than you'd think.
reviews.author: David R.

reviews.quote: We coordinate from Australia. Nurse reviews every few months and we get notes. Visits when we're home look good — can't ask for more from abroad.
reviews.author: Karen M.

midlothian.quote: Quick setup after Dad's fall. Nurse in Dalkeith was thorough. Same carer since February — he's much steadier on his feet now.
midlothian.author: Helen B.

midlothian.quote: Nurse visit in Penicuik to build Mum's routine made a difference. Carers are gentle and on time. One swap took a week to sort, but resolved fine.
midlothian.author: Douglas T.

midlothian.quote: Used respite in Bonnyrigg twice. Knowing there's clinical backup lets us actually switch off for a few days.
midlothian.author: Morag K.

eastLothian.quote: Assumed we'd be an afterthought out in North Berwick. Wasn't the case — thorough assessment and carer's never late in eight months.
eastLothian.author: Iain M.

eastLothian.quote: Personal care in Haddington was a slog to arrange elsewhere. Nurse-led plan here and Dad feels treated with respect. That's what mattered.
eastLothian.author: Fiona G.

eastLothian.quote: Musselburgh team were kind after Dad's hospital stay. Nurse oversight helped. Paperwork side was a bit slow, care side was good.
eastLothian.author: Graeme S.

westLothian.quote: Managing from Australia isn't easy. Nurse reviews in Livingston and regular updates help. Mum seems well when we visit.
westLothian.author: Karen M.

westLothian.quote: Carer in Linlithgow for Dad — patient, on time, no drama. Does what it says on the tin.
westLothian.author: Robert C.

westLothian.quote: Short-notice respite in Bathgate. Nurse visit was reassuring. Would use again if we needed cover.
westLothian.author: Shona W.

reviews.quote: Weeks trying to find care in Crieff. Colleague mentioned Zento — nurse visit within a week. Local High Street office makes a difference.
reviews.author: Susan T.

reviews.quote: Comrie felt like it would be awkward to arrange. Wasn't. Nurse knew her stuff, same weekly carer since. Finally feels managed.
reviews.author: Ian F.

reviews.quote: Mum home from Ninewells needing support fast. Carer next day, proper plan within the week. Nurse-led bit stops me worrying about meds.
reviews.author: Patricia L.

crieff.quote: Couldn't find decent home care in Crieff for weeks. Zento had a nurse out within days. East High Street office is handy for popping in.
crieff.author: Susan T.

crieff.quote: Post-hospital support for Mum was urgent. Carer next day, plan within the week. Still a worrying time, but we weren't left hanging.
crieff.author: Patricia L.

crieff.quote: Dependable carers who get Dad's quirks. Rural cover can be patchy everywhere — here it's been consistent.
crieff.author: Alistair M.

comrie.quote: Expected arranging care in Comrie to be a faff. Nurse assessment was straightforward, same carer every week since.
comrie.author: Ian F.

comrie.quote: St Fillans in winter — worried about missed visits. Haven't had one yet. Local team seems to plan routes properly.
comrie.author: Catriona D.

comrie.quote: Post-op recovery at home. Clinical oversight helped and office answers the phone. Mum's doing alright.
comrie.author: Alan W.
